title: Surface contracts for ephemeral open variants and compatibility signals
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We regularly ingest community / open-source model variants that teams want available quickly for customers, but many of these are deployed without a stable version pin. Without a clear contract for 'ephemeral' or unpinned variants, runtime teams are forced into ad-hoc fallbacks, customer teams see surprising model behavior changes, and cost/reliability regressions are harder to attribute.

Goal: Define a concise onboarding declaration and fallback contract for unpinned (ephemeral) open-model variants that we will surface in the catalog UI and intake forms. The contract should set minimum runtime assurances (latency profile, quantization compatibility notes, expected sequence-length behavior), a required set of compat signals for the runtime to use for auto-routing/fallback, and a clear rollout/failover policy that the catalog can orchestrate. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, and a proposed rollout plan for PM -> Eng -> Design handoff.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Catalog intake form includes an explicit 'variant stability' chooser (pinned | soft-pinned | ephemeral) with helper text and required compatibility fields.
2) For ephemeral variants, intake requires a small compatibility payload: supported precisions (fp16/INT8), tested max sequence length, recommended quantization profile, and a one-line known-incompatibilities note.
3) Runtime must be able to consume the compat signals to map requests to the nearest compatible model variant or trigger fallback. Mock-up API contract documented in Confluence and reviewed by serving-runtime.
4) UI surfaces the variant's contract to customers and shows a tooltip with fallback behavior (e.g., auto-route to pinned sibling, degrade-quality but preserve latency).
5) Operational playbook created: how to roll back, how to mark ephemeral variants as deprecated, and how to escalate P0 regressions.
6) Integration smoke tests covering one ephemeral variant demonstrate fallback to pinned variant under load in dedicated test environment.
decisions:
- Use a three-state stability enum: pinned / soft-pinned / ephemeral.
- Ephemeral variants default to time-limited catalog entries (90 days) unless promoted.
- Compatibility payload limited to five fields to avoid blocking quick intake.
- Runtime will prefer 'pinned' siblings for strict compatibility failures, and 'soft-pinned' for approximate matches if latency budget allows.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Drafted intake form and compatibility payload fields; shared with Eng (runtime) for initial feasibility feedback.
2026-02-24: Runtime team confirmed compat fields can be consumed; requested clarifications on quantization profile naming conventions.
2026-03-02: Design produced a lightweight tooltip and intake microcopy; PM reviewed for legal/claims language.
2026-03-09: Security requested KMS audit note for private weights ingestion; added to dependencies.
2026-03-10: Handoff doc prepared for initial implementation sprint; awaiting ENG prioritization.
notes: Key UX constraint: language must avoid implying model quality guarantees for ephemeral variants. Legal suggested 'best-effort' phrasing and a visible 'not for production' indicator unless promoted. Runtime asked for a machine-readable compat payload (json schema) but requested it be minimal to avoid blocking community submissions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): add enum and compat fields to intake API; show flag in catalog without customer-visible tooltip. Phase 2 (1 sprint): integrate runtime fallback mapping in staging and run smoke tests. Phase 3 (1 sprint): enable UI tooltip, add time-limited ephemeral tag, and publish operational playbook. Monitor for 4 weeks, then evaluate metrics for promotion to pinned process.
